LESSON 1
The Seven Elements of Art
Instructional Content · Week 1: Learn & Look
📖 ESSENTIAL QUESTION
Every work of art ever made is built from the same seven simple parts. What are they — and can you learn to see them anywhere?
Painters, sculptors, and printmakers do not start with a blank mind. They start with a toolkit called the Elements of Art: line, shape, form, color, value, texture, and space. Learn to name these seven, and you will never look at a picture the same way again.
🎯 BY THE END OF THIS LESSON YOU WILL BE ABLE TO…
1
I will be able to name and define all seven Elements of Art.
2
I will be able to find each element at work inside a real masterwork.
3
I will be able to plan a drawing that shows all seven elements on one page.
👀 PART 1 · LOOK FIRST

Before we name anything, let's look.

This is one of the most loved night scenes ever painted. A Dutch artist named Vincent van Gogh painted it outdoors, at night, on a café terrace in the town of Arles in southern France in 1888. Spend a full minute looking before you read on.

🧠 SEE · NOTICE · WONDER

👀 What do you SEE? A café terrace glowing golden-yellow under a big lantern at night. People sit at round tables out front. A cobblestone street runs back into the town under a deep blue, star-filled sky.

🔍 What do you NOTICE? The warm yellow of the café pops against the cool blue night. Your eye gets pulled down the street into the distance. There is no black anywhere, even the shadows are blue and violet.

💭 What do you WONDER? How did Van Gogh make a night scene feel warm and glowing instead of dark and gloomy? By the end of this lesson, you will be able to answer that — using the seven Elements of Art.

📚 PART 2 · NAME WHAT YOU SEE

The Seven Elements of Art

The Elements of Art are the seven basic ingredients an artist uses to make any artwork. Watch for each one inside Café Terrace at Night.

✏️
LINE — a path made by a moving point. Lines can be thick or thin, straight or curved. In the café: the straight edges of the buildings and window frames, and the long lines of the street, guide your eye.
△
SHAPE — a flat, two-dimensional area with edges. Shapes are geometric (circles, rectangles) or organic (free, natural). In the café: the round table tops are geometric; the big sweeping awning is a free organic shape.
🎲
FORM — a shape that looks three-dimensional: it has height, width, AND depth. On flat canvas, artists fake form with shading. In the café: the tables, chairs, and figures look solid and rounded, not flat.
🎨
COLOR — what we see when light bounces off a surface. In the café: Van Gogh set a warm yellow-orange terrace against a deep blue sky. Blue and orange are opposite colors, so each one looks even stronger.
◑
VALUE — how light or dark something is. In the café: the glowing bright terrace stands against the dark buildings and shadowed street, a strong jump from light to dark.
🬧
TEXTURE — the way a surface feels, or looks like it would feel. In the café: Van Gogh laid the paint on thick, so the brushstrokes stand up in rough ridges you can almost feel.
🗺️
SPACE — the area around, between, and behind things, including the illusion of depth. In the café: the cobblestone street grows narrower as it runs back, so the terrace feels close and the town feels far away.
A quick look at VALUE — value is how light or dark something is. Look how the bright lit café front sits right beside the dark shadowed doorway:

🔎 PART 3 · WATCH IT WORK

How an artist reads a picture

Artists look in a careful order: first they describe, then they analyze, then they interpret, and only then do they judge. Watch how it works on Café Terrace at Night.

DESCRIBE — what is there? A yellow café terrace with tables and people sits on the left; a cobblestone street runs down the middle into town; a deep blue sky full of stars spreads overhead.
ANALYZE — how is it built? Warm yellow color glows against the cool blue night; the street's lines open up deep space; thick brushstroke texture covers the surface; a big value jump sets the lit terrace against the dark buildings.
INTERPRET — what might it mean? The scene feels warm, calm, and welcoming, an ordinary café turned into a cozy, glowing haven under a vast, peaceful night.
JUDGE — does it succeed? Most viewers say yes: Van Gogh turned a small street café into one of the most loved night scenes ever painted.
💡 YOUR TURN IS COMING

This week you will make an Elements All-in-One Drawing — one big drawing split into sections, each section showing a different element. The seven tools you just met in Café Terrace at Night are the same seven you will put to work yourself.

⚠️ WORTH KNOWING · AI & ART
An AI image generator can make a finished-looking picture from a few words in seconds. It cannot build the trained eye that notices line, value, and space, or the hand that puts them on paper. That part is yours to develop.
📚 VOCABULARY
Line
A path made by a moving point.
Shape
A flat area with edges; geometric or organic.
Form
A 3-D shape with height, width, and depth.
Color
What we see when light reflects off a surface.
Value
How light or dark something is.
Texture
How a surface feels, or looks like it would feel.
Space
The area around and between things; near vs. far.
Impasto
Paint laid on thick, so the brushstrokes stand up and add texture.

💪 THE BIG IDEA

Seven elements — line, shape, form, color, value, texture, space — build every artwork you will ever see. Learn to name them, and you have the artist's alphabet. The rest of this course is learning to spell.
